course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 9

unit.title: Shapes and Measurements
unit.blurb: Circumference and area of circles and parts of circles, areas of compound shapes, and converting between large and small units of area and volume.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Know and use the formulae for the circumference (C = πd = 2πr) and area (A = πr²) of a circle, including semicircles and quarter circles.

O2.t: Find the area and perimeter of compound shapes made from rectangles, triangles, trapezia and parts of circles.

O3.t: Convert between units of length, area (mm², cm², m², km², hectares) and volume (mm³, cm³, m³, litres).

sections.title: Circumference and area of a circle

p: The **circumference** is the distance round a circle: **C = πd = 2πr**.
The **area** is **A = πr²**. Always use the radius for the area – halve the diameter first.
π ≈ 3.14159… Use the π button and round only at the end.

p: A **compound shape** is made of simpler shapes. **Split** it into rectangles, triangles, trapezia or parts of circles, find each area, then **add** (or **subtract** a hole).
Useful formulae: rectangle lw; triangle ½bh; parallelogram bh; trapezium ½(a + b)h.

p: 1 m² = 100 × 100 = **10 000 cm²**; 1 m³ = **1 000 000 cm³**; 1 km² = 1 000 000 m²; 1 **hectare** = 10 000 m². For capacity: **1 cm³ = 1 mL** and **1000 cm³ = 1 litre**.
